4. Brief facts, leading to the filing of present appeals, before this Court, may be summed up as under:-
4.1.

Petitioners, being successors of deceased Hem Raj, have filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as the 'M.V.
Act'), against the respondents, being owner, driver and insurer of offending vehicle.
4.2. During the pendency of the lis before the learned Tribunal, respondent No.1 had died and his legal heirs i.e. respondents No. 1(a) to 1(d), were impleaded, in the claim petition.

4.3. Elaborating their stand, it is the case of the petitioner that on 23.03.2004, Hem Raj @ Himmat Ram, .
along with Sanjay Kumar @ Sanju, had hired the offending vehicle, in order to carry their domestic and occupational goods, purchased from Pandoh and after loading the goods, they were travelling,
in the offending vehicle, as care taker of of their goods, as they were also to unload the goods, at the destination.

When, the offending vehicle, being driven by respondent No.2, reached at the place known as 'Surahi khud' at about 7.30 p.m., respondent No.2, lost control over it, due to rash and negligent driving, and the offending vehicle rolled down from the road, in the 400 deep gorge.
Consequently, Sanjay Kumar and Hem Raj, died on the spot, whereas, driver and cleaner, had sustained injuries.

The postmortem examination of Shri Hem Raj was conducted at Zonal Hospital,
Mandi on 24.03.2004.
4.5.

The information regarding the accident was given to the Police of Police Station, Gohar, where,
FIR No.47 of 2004, under Sections 279, 337 and 304A IPC, was registered.
The age of Hem Raj, at the time of his death, has been pleaded, as 28 years.
He was stated to be agriculturist and Carpenter by profession and earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
The petitioners have pleaded about their bright past and bleak future.

. 
5. On the basis of above facts, the petitioners have sought the compensation, on account of death of Shri Hem Raj, in the said accident, involving the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 6. When put to notice, the claim petition has been contested by the respondents, by filing their separate rt replies.

7. Respondent No.1 has filed his reply, by pleading that although, the accident has been taken place,
but, according to him, the same had not taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2.
He has admitted the registration of the FIR, but, stated that the same has been based upon the wrong facts.
Elaborating his stand, it has been pleaded that the accident, in question, had taken place due to the breakage of tie rod end of the offending vehicle.
He has also denied that both the persons were travelling, in the vehicle, as care taker of the goods.
8. Respondent No.2 has filed his reply, in which, he has also taken, almost the same stand.

But,
according to him, the occupants were engaged by him, for the purpose of loading and unloading the goods.

At the same time, he has denied that those persons were travelling in the vehicle, as .
care taker of the goods.

9. The Insurance-Company has filed its separate reply by taking preliminary objections that the offending vehicle was being permitted to ply, in violation of the terms of and conditions of the Insurance policy; and that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle, as a rt gratuitous passenger.
On merits, the contents of the petition, have been denied, mainly, for want of knowledge.
10. Thus, the respondents have prayed for the dismissal of the claim petition.

11. On the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed by the learned Tribunal vide order dated 04.01.2006:-
1.

Whether deceased (Hem Raj alias Himat Ram) died on account of injuries sustained by him due to the rash and negligent driving of Truck No.HP09-0735 on 23.03.2004 at about 7.30 p.m., at village Surahi Khad on Pandoh-Gohar Road, being driven by respondent No.2 as alleged?

OPP. 
2. If issue No.1 is proved in affirmative to what amount of compensation, the petitioners are entitled to and from whom ?

OPP. 
3. Whether respondent No.2 was not having a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident?
OPR-3.

4. Whether deceased was travelling in the offending truck as a gratuitous passenger if so to what effect? OPR-3.
5.
Relief.

13. After the closure of evidence and after hearing of learned counsel for the parties, the learned Tribunal has allowed the petition, as referred to above, by exonerating the Insurance-Company.

14. rt Feeling aggrieved from the said award, the present appeal has been filed before this Court,
assailing the award, mainly, on the ground that the petitioner has miserably failed to prove the fact that the accident, in question, had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2.
15.

The award has also been assailed on the ground that the learned Tribunal, has given the undue weightage to the statement of PW-2 Ved Kumar, as RW-2, has specifically stated that when, the offending vehicle reached, at the place of accident, the tie rod has been broken and the accident took place.

16. The award has also been assailed on the ground that the learned Tribunal has not given any reason to disbelieve the statement of Govind Ram, and undue weightage has been given to the statement of RW-4 Mohan Lal.

The findings have further been assailed, on the ground that the learned Tribunal, has wrongly held that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger, whereas, the Insurance Company could not substantiate the stand, by of leading any cogent evidence.

18. The learned Tribunal, according to respondent rt No.1, has wrongly held that Hem Raj was a gratuitous passenger, whereas, PW-2 Ved Kumar, has specifically stated that at the place of accident, rice, wheat and pulses were found scattered and one new bedding was also found there.

19. The findings have further been assailed on the ground that it has been probabilized, in this case,
that the deceased was travelling in the vehicle, as care taker of the goods and he has also to load the peas crop.

20. On the basis of above facts, Ms. Anu Tuli Azta, Advocate, has argued that the appeal may kindly be accepted and the impugned award may kindly be set aside, by dismissing the claim petition.
21.

It has also been argued that in case, this Court comes to the conclusion that the petition is not liable to be dismissed, then, the liability to pay the compensation, if .
any, should be saddled upon the Insurance Company, being insurer of the offending vehicle, at the relevant time, as no fundamental breach of insurance policy has been proved or probabilized by the Insurance-Company.

Per contra, Mr. B.M. Chauhan, learned Senior Advocate assisted rt by Mr. Amit Himalvi,
Advocate, appeareing for respondents No.3-Insurance Company, has supported the award passed by the learned Tribunal, by arguing that the learned Tribunal has rightly held that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle, as gratuitous passenger and as such, it has been proved, in this case, that the offending vehicle was being permitted to ply, in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
23.

Mr. G.R. Palsra, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, has argued that the compensation, which has been awarded by the learned Tribunal, is on the lower side and the same does not fall within the definition of 'just compensation'.
24. On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to enhance the amount, by putting the liability to pay the amount of compensation, on the Insurance .
Company.

25. In order to decide the controversy involved in the present case, it would be just and appropriate for this Court to discuss the oral, as well as, documentary evidence of adduced by the parties, before the learned Tribunal.

26. After framing of issues, the petitioners have rt examined Dr. D.P. Handa, Medical Officer, Zonal Hospital, Mandi, as PW-1, who has conducted the postmortem examination of the dead body of Hem Raj and proved the copy of the postmortem report, as Ext.PW-1/A.
27. PW-2, Ved Kumar, at the relevant time, was Pradhan of Gram Panchayat, Chhaprahan.

According to him, at about 7.00-7.30 p.m., on 23.03.2004, he received a telephonic call from Dalip Kumar, informing him that one vehicle had met with an accident, at Surahi Khad, upon which, he had informed the police on phone and reached at the spot.
When, he had reached at the spot, he noticed that Sanjay Kumar was dead, whereas, Hem Raj, cleaner of the truck and driver were lying there, in injured conditions.
The damaged vehicle was there on the spot.
Rice, flour, cereals, were found scattered there.
One new bedding was also there.
The flour and rice were delivered at the house of Hem Raj, on the next day.
In the hospital, when, the driver of the offending vehicle was inquired about the said articles, he has told that the same were of Hem Raj and Sanjay Kumar.
Consequently, those articles were delivered to them.
of Thereafter, the injured were taken to Mandi.
Truck driver also disclosed that at Chhaparahan, he had to load the peas rt crop belonging to Sanjay, Hem Raj and other persons.
In the Hospital, Hem Raj also succumbed to the injuries.

while driving the offending vehicle, he was on the way from Daralaghat to Kullu.

40. In the cross-examination, this witness has admitted that he does not know, as, in which capacity,
deceased were travelling in the vehicle.
This fact has not been inquired from any witness as he has to inquire about the fact whether the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner.
He has reached at the spot, after one hour from the accident.
The place of accident was a gorge.
He has admitted that the place of accident being gorge, as such, no efforts were made to ascertain the goods, as their first preference was to provide treatment to the injured.
However, Pradhan Ved Ram has disclosed that the deceased were to load the peas at Chhaprahan, as such, the vehicle was hired.
However, he has feigned his ignorance about the fact, as to whether they had loaded some articles from Pandoh.

41. When this witness has reached at the spot, the .
injured were already taken to hospital.
However, dead body of Sanjay was lying there on the spot.
When, he along with other police officials reached at the spot, it was already dark.
He has feigned his ignorance that the persons of gathered there had delivered the articles to the rightful owners.
He has admitted that Ved Ram has disclosed to rt him that on the spot a new beddings and the sack of rice and cereals were found.
42. This is the entire evidence led by the parties to the petition.

43. In this case, learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.4,79,000/- along-with interest @ 7.5%
per annum.
However, the liability has been fastened upon respondents No. 1 and 2 by exonerating the Insurance-Company.
The petitioner has not assailed the award.

44. Petitioners have categorically pleaded in the petition that Hem Raj @ Himmat Ram had hired the offending vehicle along-with one Sanjay @ Sanju, in order to carry various kind of domestic and occupational goods, purchased at Pandoh and they were travelling in the truck as care taker of those goods.
45. This stand has been denied by the respondents.
The Insurance-Company has not sought any permission under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
Petitioner No.1, in this case, has deposed, in her examination-in-chief that on that day, her husband had gone to Pandoh in order of to purchase some articles.
On that day, he had to sell the peas crop.
Lastly, she has deposed that on the next day of rt the incident, her co-villager had handed over flour and rice, which her husband had purchased and was carrying the same in the truck.

48. Not only this, PW-3 has also probabilized the .
stand of the petitioner qua the fact that her husband was travelling in the offending vehicle as owner of the goods.
49. RW-1 Roshan Lal (respondent No.1), is the owner of the offending vehicle.
He has deposed on the basis of of information given to him by respondent No.2, qua the fact that the offending vehicle was hired by three persons for rt carrying peas crop from Chapran.
The said crop was to be transported to Sundernagar vegetable market.
Hem Raj and Sanjay had loaded their domestic articles in the vehicle and on the way, the vehicle met with an accident.
RW-2 Govind Ram is the person, who was on the wheels of the offending vehicle, at the relevant time.

He has deposed about the fact that on 23.03.2004, when, he was on the way to Darlaghat, when, he had reached at Pandoh and stopped the vehicle in order to have tea, in the meanwhile, Brij Lal, peas trader and two other persons, namely, Hem Raj and Sanjay came to him.
Brij Lal has requested him to carry the peas crop from Chapran to Sundernagar, upon which, he has requested Brij Lal to arrange for the labour.
It is his further case that Hem Raj and Sanjay had agreed to load the peas crop and they have also loaded some domestic articles such as quilt, cereals and rice etc., in the offending vehicle.

Both of them had agreed to pay the rent and .
thereafter, they had loaded the articles in the offending vehicle and travelled in the same as owner/care taker of those articles.
Brij Lal had proceeded towards Chapran on his scooter.
of 50.
In cross-examination by learned counsel for the Insurance-Company, he has deposed that deceased were rt travelling in the rear portion of the vehicle along-with their articles.
RW-4, who is the I.O has also deposed that Ved Ram, Pradhan has disclosed him that on the spot one new bedding, few sacks of rice and cereals were found on the spot.
51. The proceedings under the M.V. Act are summary in nature, where, the liability of the tort-feaser can be fixed, on the principle of preponderance of probability.
Strict Rules of Evidence Act are not applicable to the summary proceedings under the M.V. Act.
Since, the proceedings are summary in nature, as such, pleadings are also not liable to be strictly construed.

If the submissions as made by learned counsel for the Insurance-Company are taken to be correct, that evidence of RW-1 and RW-2 is beyond their pleadings, even then, there is no legal impediment for the petitioners to rely Chunni Lal And Others vs Lata Devi & And Others on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142927693/
9 upon the evidence of RW-1 and RW-2.

sentences.text:
The bar with regard to the consideration of evidence beyond .
pleadings will only applicable against respondents No. 1 and 2 and not against the petitioners.
52. While deciding the question, involved in the lis, entire evidence adduced by the parties is to be taken into of consideration.
Opportunity of cross-examination has also been given to the Insurance-Company, respondent No.3 to rt cross-examine RW-1 and RW-2.
It has also not been suggested to them that the evidence given by them is in order to help the petitioner, rather it has been suggested to RW-2 that he is deposing, in order to save his owner.
Despite of lengthy cross-examination, nothing material could be elicited from him, from which, an adverse inference could be drawn that these witnesses are deposing in order to help the petitioner.
It has also not been suggested that they are in collusion with the petitioner.

53. From the evidence of RW-1, RW-2 and RW-4, the petitioners have probabilized their case that her husband had purchased the domestic articles from Pandoh and after loading the same, he was travelling with those articles as owner of the goods.

In such a situation, the learned Tribunal has erroneously exonerated the Insurance-Company by holding that the Insurance-Company is not liable to pay the compensation, as Hem Raj @ Himmat Ram was travelling in .
the vehicle as a gratuitous passenger.
54. The term 'gratuitous passenger' has no where been defined in M.V. Act, but it means one who has taken the lift.

The learned counsel for appearing for the of Insurance-Company could not satisfy the judicial conscience of this Court as to how, the learned Tribunal has held that rt deceased was a gratuitous passenger, as, it has been probabilized, in this case, that deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle as owner-cum-care taker of the goods.
55. The learned trial Court, in this case, has exonerated the Insurance-Company and saddled the liability to pay compensation, along-with interest, on the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
The said findings are not sustainable in the eyes of law as considering the low legal literacy rate of Indian masses, it cannot expected from them to purchase the articles against the bills.

The deceased was residing in village Chapran, Tehsil Chachiot, District Mandi, H.P., and generally, people of the said area are simpleton in nature and not aware about the fact that the bills/cash memos are required to be obtained.
The hyper technical approach as adopted by the learned Tribunal is not sustainable, keeping in view the fact that normally no-one insists upon the seller to issue cash memos or bills.

The .
evidence of the parties has to be considered as a whole.
56. It is the specific case of the petitioners, in the claim petition, that Hem Raj and Sanjay Kumar had hired the offending vehicle for loading the goods.

This stand has of not only been supported by Chunni Lal And Others vs Lata Devi & And Others on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142927693/
10 the driver, but he has moved a step further by deposing that one Brij Lal had also hired and rt negotiated him to transport the peas crop from village Chapran to Sundernagar vegetable market.

sentences.text: The peas season was there, at the relevant time, as such, if the evidence of the parties, so adduced, is examined, on the touch stone of preponderance of probability, then, the case is made out that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle as owner-cum-care taker of the goods.
Not only this, he had to load his peas crop and peas crop of Brij Lal, which was to be transported in the offending vehicle.

57. The award is totally silent as to how the deceased was a gratuitous passenger, whereas, it is the specific stand of the petitioner that deceased had hired the offending vehicle for transporting his household goods.

This fact has also been probabilized from the evidence of PW-2 Ved Kumar, as well as, RW-4 Mohan Lal, the I.O.
58.

A Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in a decision .
dated 22.08.2014 rendered in FAO No. 9 of 2017 a/w FAO No. 226 of 2007 has held that owner of goods cannot be said to be gratuitous passenger.

The relevant Paras 14 to 19 of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
of "14.
I have gone through the pleadings and the evidence led by the parties.

It is admitted by all rt the parties that the deceased has hired the vehicle for transporting his vegetables to Sabzi Mandi and was returning back to his native place in the same vehicle at the time of accident, thus, was owner of the goods, cannot be said to be gratuitous passenger.

15. This Court in a case titled as National Insurance Co. Ltd. versus Kamla and others, reported in 2011 ACJ 1550, has also discussed the same issue while referring to the judgment of the Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd.

The relevant paragraphs 17 and 20 of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"17.
By reason of the 1994 Amendment what was added is "including the owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicle".

The liability of the owner of the vehicle to insure it compulsorily, thus, by reason of the aforementioned amendment included only the owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicle besides the third parties.

The intention of the Parliament,
therefore, could not have been that the words 'any person' occurring in Section 147 would cover all persons who were travelling in a goods .
carriage in any capacity whatsoever.

If such was the intention there was no necessity of the Parliament to carry out an amendment inasmuch as expression 'any person'
contained in sub-clause (i) of clause (b) of sub- section (1) of Section 147 would have included the owner of the goods or his authorised representative of besides the passengers who are gratuitous or otherwise.

sentences.text: 20. It is therefore, manifest that in spite of the amendment of 1994, the effect of the provision rt contained in Section 147 with respect to persons other than the owner of the goods or his authorized representative remains the same.
